description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three measures of accuracy—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a set of LLMs. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear scale from approximately 0.84 to 0.99, with tick labels indicating increments of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting near 1.0 and remaining relatively stable above 0.95 across the entire range of initial confidence. The “Initial Accuracy” is shown as a dashed green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 0.6, rising to a peak near 0.88 at an initial confidence of 0.88, then declining slightly before stabilizing around 0.8. The “Δ Accuracy” is depicted as a dashed orange line with diamond markers, starting near 0.5, dipping to a low of approximately 0.3 at an initial confidence of 0.86, and then rising to a peak near 0.7 before declining slightly toward 0.65. Each line is accompanied by error bars indicating variability.
